correctness.rationale: PASS. Checked exhaustive clique-type dichotomy: a cyclic-distance-k clique either sits in an interval of length k or equals one of k equilateral triangles {j,j+k,j+2k}. For arc complex A_d the new faces are uniquely indexed by their length-d endpoint edge; cone matching on interior vertex i+1 pairs every such face, has no cyclic-orbit stabilizer (n=3k>=3d), and descends as a free equivariant collapse A_k/C_n to A_1/C_n ≃ S¹. The k exceptional triangles form one rotation orbit, each with order-three stabilizer acting geometrically by an orientation-preserving triangle rotation, so contributes one disk with rim boundary 3-to-1 relative to original triangle. The original equilateral boundary traverses the full n-edge cycle once via interval faces; after the degree-n rim covering, attaching degree is n/3=k. Thus a CW circle with one 2-cell attached by k has π1 and H1=Z/k and no higher reduced homology. Independent barycentric face-flag orbit chain complexes for k=2,3 and characteristics 2,3,5 reproduce predicted Betti patterns; finite checks only test, do not replace, the all-k equivariant collapse.
